name: 2.11BSD (patch level 499)
description: The newest 2.11BSD: patch level 499 of January 2026, built by Johnny Billquist, who maintains the official 2.11BSD patches (kernel "pidp", 1 GB RA82 disk). The same system as the default 2.11BSD entry with two more years of fixes. The first boot switches on the image's automatic multi-user boot and reboots once by itself. It is downloaded by FTP from ftp.dfupdate.se; upstream regenerates that file from time to time (this entry pins the one of 27 October 2026), and when it has been replaced the checksum no longer matches and the install stops with an error.

shutdown: Log in as root and type shutdown -h now: 2.11BSD syncs the disks, prints "halting" and halts the CPU, and the machine can be switched off. Shut down OS does this for you from the login: prompt or a shell prompt: it logs in as root. At another user's shell it types nothing and says so, as while a program uses the console: log out or leave the program first.

shutdownScript.else: the console is not at a root shell or login: prompt, so nothing was typed. A program or another user's shell may be using it (its prompt > looks like a shell waiting for more input), or a command may be half typed: leave the program (vi: Esc, then :q), log out (Ctrl+D), or clear the line (Ctrl+U), press Return for a fresh prompt and try again.
the user logged in on the console did not log out: log out by hand, then try again.
the user logged in on the console has suspended jobs, so the console was not logged out: end them (fg, then leave the program), log out with Ctrl+D and try again.
the console asks for a password the script does not know: log in as root by hand, then try again.

notes:
## Log in

Log in as **root** (no password); set a password with `passwd` if others can reach this machine.

The image comes with `rc_configured=NO` in `/etc/rc.conf`, which stops the automatic multi-user boot at a root shell. On the first boot the console therefore types one command by itself: it sets `rc_configured=YES` and `sendmail=NO` in `/etc/rc.conf` and reboots. No network address is configured and the machine has no network card.

The PDP-11/70 has no battery clock and there is no network, so the clock starts at the date stored on the disk (October 2026). Set it as root with `date yymmddhhmm`, e.g. `date 2610221530`.

## Things to try

* `uname -a`, `cat /VERSION`, `df`, `ps ax`, `who`: a BSD UNIX from 1992, patched until 2026.
* Write a C program and compile it:

  ```
  cat > hello.c
  main() { printf("hello, world\n"); }
  ```

  then Ctrl+D, `cc -o hello hello.c` and `./hello`. `f77` compiles Fortran.
* Games in `/usr/games`: `adventure`, `zork`, `hack`, `trek`, `rain`, `worms`, `wump`, `backgammon`, `fortune` and more (`ls /usr/games`).
* Editors: Bill Joy's original `vi` and the Emacs-like `jove`; `man vi` shows the manual.
* The front panel: turn the DATA knob to DATA PATHS. While 2.11BSD idles, its idle loop rotates a band of 8 lit bits through R0 before every WAIT, and the panel shows R0 during WAIT. Read the idle loop in `/usr/src/sys/pdp/mch_xxx.s` (search for `rdisply`).
* The kernel configuration is `/usr/src/sys/conf/pidp`; the whole system source is in `/usr/src`.

## Shut down

As root type `shutdown -h now`. 2.11BSD stops its daemons, syncs the disks, prints "halting" and halts the CPU (HALT instruction); then switch off. If you pull the plug instead, the next boot repairs the file systems (fsck) and reboots once by itself, which takes about 35 seconds longer, up to a minute if the disks were being written (at Authentic speed 13 minutes: switch to Fast meanwhile). Files that were being written can be lost (`/lost+found`). A disk fsck cannot repair stops the boot at a root shell, with "fsck cannot repair this disk" on the console: Factory reset restores the disk.

**Shut down OS** does this for you. It starts from the `login:` prompt (a half-typed name is cleared), from a root shell, or from another user's shell, which it logs out first (it says so if suspended jobs keep the user logged in). It never types into a program: with `vi` open, a half-typed command or anything else but a prompt on the last line it stops at once and says what to do (a stop of the service or container then powers off uncleanly).

console.keyHelp: Backspace erases · Ctrl+U kills the line · Ctrl+C interrupts · Ctrl+Z suspends (csh) · Ctrl+D logs out

terminals.enableHint: /etc/ttys ships with the DZ11 lines tty00-tty07 switched off. Switch them on once as root: sed -e '/^tty0[0-7]/s/off/on/' /etc/ttys > /tmp/ttys && cp /tmp/ttys /etc/ttys && kill -HUP 1 - then telnet to the listener and log in. Log out (Ctrl+D) before closing the telnet connection: closing it hangs up the line (modem control), but 2.11BSD notices that only about once a second, and a new connection within that time gets the old, still logged-in session.
